office.name: Office of the Supervisor, Charter Township of Hampton
office.place: Hampton Charter Township, Bay County, Michigan (township hall 801 W. Center Rd., Essexville, MI 48732; borders Bay City and Essexville on Saginaw Bay)
office.remit: A Michigan charter township (Charter Township Act, PA 359 of 1947). Legislative power sits with a seven-member township board: supervisor, clerk, treasurer and four trustees (MCL 42.5). The supervisor presides over the board and is the township's chief executive and chief assessing officer (MCL 42.5, 42.10, 42.11a); in this township the supervisor is full-time and runs day-to-day administration with a deputy supervisor. The township runs a Department of Public Works (brush chipping, roadside ditching, parks, township buildings), a Public Safety Department (public safety officers for police) and a paid-on-call fire department, planning and zoning with building inspection, contract assessing, and a solid waste collection contract paid by special assessment on the winter tax bill. The clerk (elected) runs elections, minutes and records; the treasurer (elected) collects taxes. Roads in the township are county roads under the Bay County Road Commission; the township pays for local road work by agreement with it. Water and sewer systems are township-owned but operated by Bay County's Department of Water and Sewer since January 2024. The township board approves contracts, budgets, special assessment rolls and purchases over the purchasing policy limit.

succession.rule: MCL 168.370(1): a vacancy in an elective township office is filled by appointment by the township board, and the appointee holds office for the remainder of the unexpired term; 168.370(4): if the board does not fill it within 45 days, the county clerk calls a special election. MCL 168.370a shortens the appointee's term only when the vacancy occurs more than 7 days before the nominating petition deadline for an intervening general November election; a vacancy in September 2026 falls after the 2026 filing deadline, so the appointee serves until the regular 2028 election (township officers are elected in presidential years for four-year terms, MCL 168.358). Revised Statutes of 1846, MCL 41.56: a resignation is in writing to the township board, filed with the clerk, and effective when accepted by the board. MCL 42.5: a board member who wants the appointment may abstain; the appointee must be an elector of the township. Oath before the clerk, MCL 168.363.
succession.timeline: Thu Sept 3, 2026: the previous supervisor delivers a written resignation to the clerk (no reason given). Tue Sept 8: regular board meeting (moved from Labor Day) accepts it; vacancy begins; Trustee Ed Borowicz chosen president pro tem; letters of interest due Wed Sept 16. Mon Sept 21: special meeting, four applicants interviewed; Tom Seidlitz appointed 5-1. Tue Sept 22, 9:00 a.m.: oath before the clerk; bond filed. Term runs to the start of the term elected in November 2028.
